slides.title: Parameters and Arguments
slides.content: Parameters are placeholders in the method definition. Arguments are the real values passed when calling the method.

slides.title: Return Values
slides.content: The return type defines what the method gives back. Use return to send a value, or void for no return.

slides.title: Named Arguments
slides.content: Named arguments let you specify which parameter gets which value by writing the parameter name.

slides.title: Default Parameters
slides.content: Default parameters have preset values. You can omit them when calling, and the default is used.

slides.title: Multiple Parameters
slides.content: Methods can take any number of parameters. Separate them with commas in the definition and call.

slides.title: Parameter Types
slides.content: Parameters can be value types, reference types, arrays, or even other methods. The type must be specified.

slides.title: Optional and Required
slides.content: Parameters with default values are optional. Those without defaults are required. Optional parameters must come after required ones.
slides.exampleOutput:
Alice 18 Unknown
Bob 25 Unknown
Charlie 30 NYC

slides.title: Best Practices
slides.content: Use meaningful parameter names. Keep parameter count reasonable. Prefer named arguments for clarity with many parameters.
